chapter: Europe and the Black and Blue years
title: European fans: loyal and generous
summary: Starting on fans, Humes says European audiences are completely in your corner. In Sweden everything was paid for, and a driver and chauffeur looked after her.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Okay Helen, now let's talk about fans and the difference between the kind of fan that you encountered in France and the kind of fan that you encountered in America and the kind of fan that you encountered in Europe; we probably better talk about European fans first. (Laughter)
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, when people over there like you they are really in your corner a hundred percent. And I've got so many fans and friends and things that I still hear from.
Yes. And they are such wonderful people.
They really love you, don't they?

Yeah. And they are just so kind and they just try to, you know - I went to Sweden and that was the first time I ever went anyplace -- and I didn't even know what kind of money they had there. I didn't spend nothing. Not a nickel. And I said, well, if I wanted lunch they would send out and get me lunch. And they'd send a car to the hotel to take me here and take me there. Or if I wanted to go see something, or if I wanted to buy something the chauffeur would buy it. And I said, well, this is the best I've ever had. The best I've ever seen.
